items.original_title: FinancialJuice: MUFG on BoC & CAD

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: MUFG on BoC & CAD
evidence.snippet: The Canadian dollar has continued to rebound against the US dollar resulting in USD/CAD hitting a low yesterday at 1.4071 as it moves further below the high from 14th October at 1.4300. The Canadian dollar has outperformed recently alongside the other G10 commodity currencies of the Norwegian krone and New Zealand dollar. The one exception has been the Australin dollar which has bene the worst performing G10 currency perhaps reflecting its tighter link to AI related demand. The recent wobble for Al-related trades may have weighed more on the Aussie than other G10 commodity currencies. The Canadian dollar has been boosted by the hawkish repricing of BoC rate hike expectations. The Candina rate market has moved to more fully price in a 25bps hike as soon as next week. There are currently around 21bps of hikes priced in compared to only 9bps at the end of last week. Those expectations have been encouraged by three major Canadian banks all changing their rate calls to a hike at next week’s policy meeting. The latest inflation data from Canada released yesterday was mixed with headline and core inflation measures coming in a little softer than consensus forecasts at around 3.1% and 1.9% respectively in September. The BoC also released its latest business and consumer outlook surveys which found that households’ longer-term inflation expectations are rising. Roughly half of the businesses surveyed also plan to pass along some or all of their cost increases from higher energy prices and tariffs to customers.

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: Standard Charted on US Midterm Potential Market Reactions

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Standard Charted on US Midterm Potential Market Reactions
evidence.snippet: A Republican sweep has an 8-10% probability but would have the most immediate asset market impact Rates and the USD would likely rise, although fiscal uncertainty would also increase Markets would likely prefer an outcome signalling dissatisfaction with both parties’ extremes If this <10% probability of a Republican sweep emerges as the outcome, we would expect to see higher rates and a stronger USD. The higher rates would reflect Republicans’ inability to rein in deficits over the past two years, the unexpected increase in military spending, the shortfall in tariff revenues, and the promise of a USD 5k dividend to adult US citizens. We also reiterate our pessimism on profit-driven economic growth leading to big revenue gains. Asset markets may still see the Republicans as growth friendly but that is not the same as believing that serious measures to reduce deficits will be undertaken. The USD could well benefit from this upward rates move. However, in our view, any USD strength would be contingent on markets expecting the Fed to keep inflation low and real rates high. items.original_title: FinancialJuice: Mizuho on US CPI and BoJ

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Mizuho on US CPI and BoJ
evidence.snippet: Although the September US CPI came in stronger than expected, it did not necessarily provide compelling evidence that inflationary pressures are broadening and is therefore unlikely to force the Fed to move up the timing of its next rate hike. Our main scenario remains that the FOMC will leave rates on hold in October. Even if the Fed were to hike in October, we think the likelihood of the BOJ also raising rates that month is low, given that it continues to characterize back-to-back rate hikes strictly as an “emergency response.” The UST curve underwent a bull flattening in the latter half of the week, apparently in part because of the decline in equity prices. However, as rates continue to trend lower even after the stock market rebound, we think the term-premium-driven rise in rates may be unwinding, which is likely to be broadly positive for JGB market sentiment. However, yen rates appear to have been relatively unaffected by the previous rise in US term premia, suggesting that downward pressure on yen rates may be limited when that move reverses. SHORT-TERM OUTLOOK (ONE WEEK - ONE MONTH) In Japan, with the market largely expecting the BOJ to forgo a hike in October and to raise rates in December, monetary policy expectations are likely to remain stable barring a surprise such as indications of an October rate hike. Together with the aforementioned reversal of the term-premium-driven rise in overseas rates, this should be broadly supportive of the market. However, to the extent that the rise in US term premia had a relatively limited impact on yen rates, a reversal of that rise may conversely also have a limited impact. In view of that and the lingering uncertainty over fiscal policy, we do not anticipate a sharp decline in yields.
